reason: This passage (Exodus 3) describes God calling Moses to liberate the Hebrew people from Egyptian oppression. The text explicitly states that God has heard the cry of the Israelites and seen their suffering (צַעֲקַת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל - 'the cry of the children of Israel' and הַלַּחַץ - 'the oppression'). Moses is being commissioned by God to lead the people out of Egypt to serve God on Mount Sinai. There is no depiction of Hebrew leaders being antagonistic to the Hebrew people; rather, the narrative shows a leader (Moses) being divinely appointed to help his oppressed people. The passage contains no evidence of antagonism between Hebrew leaders and the people.
